title: Cross-Workspace Pipeline Orchestration (Hub and Spoke)
summary: Orchestrate Fabric pipelines across workspaces with a hub master pipeline that invokes spoke pipelines: identity, control flow, central logging, CI/CD, alternatives and a hands-on workshop.
audience: Data engineers, platform architects, DevOps engineers

pages.title: Overview
pages.description: Why hub-and-spoke orchestration exists, when to use it, what the current platform supports and how this playbook is organized.

pages.title: Hub-and-spoke architecture
pages.description: Hub and spoke roles, the contract between them, how to cut spokes, and the capacity and permission model.

pages.title: The Invoke pipeline activity
pages.description: Legacy versus new activity, connections and identities, wait on completion, parameters, limits, known issues and the REST fallback.

pages.title: Control flow and failure handling
pages.description: Sequential, parallel, conditional and metadata-driven patterns, retries, timeouts, failure semantics, idempotency and run conditions.

pages.title: Logging, monitoring and CI/CD
pages.description: Central run logging, Monitoring hub, workspace monitoring, alerts, the item-ID problem and deploying hub and spokes across environments.

pages.title: Alternatives and recommendations
pages.description: Decision table comparing hub-and-spoke pipelines with notebook DAGs, Airflow jobs, event-driven triggers and run conditions, plus recommendations and a readiness checklist.

pages.title: Workshop: build hub and spokes
pages.description: Numbered hands-on exercise: two spoke workspaces, a hub workspace, a master pipeline, permissions, a test run and a troubleshooting table.
